kirkpatrick_2012.locator: Results › Plasma Methamphetamine and d-Amphetamine Levels; Results › Cardiovascular Effects › Acute Effects; Figure 1
kirkpatrick_2012.extracted: Plasma concentrations of both drugs peaked 3–4 h after dosing; cardiovascular effects peaked within 15 min (13 men).
No F statistics or degrees of freedom are printed for any analysis, and the pre-session urine screen excluded amphetamines, so recent use before sessions cannot be ruled out.

kirkpatrick_2012.locator: Results › Cardiovascular Effects › Acute Effects; Table 2
kirkpatrick_2012.extracted: Both 50 mg/70 kg conditions raised heart rate and blood pressure above placebo and the 12 mg/70 kg conditions (p<0.01); summed 'stimulated' ratings 111 after placebo vs 320 after 50 mg/70 kg methamphetamine (13 men).
No F statistics or degrees of freedom are printed, and the tables show only items with significant effects.

volkow_2001b.extracted: Five users scanned in early abstinence (mean 3, SD 1.6 months) and again in protracted abstinence (mean 14, SD 2 months): DAT availability rose 19% in the caudate and 16% in the putamen.
The DAT increase correlated with the time between scans (r=0.92, n=5), reported with 4 degrees of freedom where n−2=3 is expected.
In 5 people rescanned after about 14 months of abstinence, transporter availability rose 16–19%.

dean_2013.extracted: Evidence for brain change during abstinence (DAT, glucose metabolism, grey matter) comes from studies of 5, 5, 10 and 12 users.
Pre–post studies without retested controls, including Wang et al. (2004), cannot separate improvement from practice or retest effects.

Of 7 well-matched cross-sectional studies, 6 found users worse on some tests; of 8 statistically controlled studies, 5 did; no matched study found users better on any test; most differences were within 1 SD.

In the one twin study (50 male pairs; 80% of the stimulant-using twins had used amphetamines), the using twins did worse on four tests (two timed attention, two psychomotor), better on one sustained-attention test, and no differently on the other nine.
In 36 users, age at first use correlated with years of education (r=−0.48) and with the shortfall of actual versus predicted education (r=−0.42).

Chronic or binge dosing produces cognitive deficits in rodents and monkeys; escalating-dose pretreatment prevented deficits in several rat studies; vervet monkeys given escalating doses still showed selective deficits that improved with abstinence.

ashok_2017.extracted: Not pooled: VMAT2 lower in methamphetamine users after 3 months (g 1.68) and higher in two early-abstinence studies (g 1.16); Kish et al. (2017) describe the same Johanson et al. study as 3 years of abstinence with a 10% reduction.
Pooled transporter availability in amphetamine-type stimulant users: g −1.47 (95% CI −1.83 to −1.10), 9 studies.

volkow_2001c.extracted: Smokers were 73% of users and 24% of controls; women 60% and 28%.

wang_2004.extracted: Thalamic change is reported as correlating with change on Timed Gait (r=0.88), Symbol Digit (r=0.96) and delayed recall (r=0.98) in the 5; read against the same people's test scores in Volkow et al. (2001b), the plotted direction cannot be reconciled with the abstract's statement that larger increases went with greater improvement (second reader's finding), and correlations in 5 people are highly unstable.

volkow_2001a.extracted: The authors note that the transporter reduction was of similar size in caudate and putamen, unlike Parkinson's disease, in which the putamen is more affected.

boileau_2016.extracted: VMAT2, a marker used for terminal integrity, was 28% higher than in controls 2.6 days after use and not different from controls after about 10 days of abstinence.

hart_2012.extracted: Animal neurotoxicity regimens typically give large bolus doses to drug-naive animals, and escalating pre-exposure can prevent the neurotoxic effects of a later binge.

hart_2012.locator: Review of the Acute Effects; Table 1 (pp. 590–591)
hart_2012.extracted: Across the controlled acute-dosing studies tabulated in Table 1, single doses (up to 50 mg/70 kg intranasal or 30 mg intravenous in the studies tested) produced no cognitive disruption and improved some domains (visuospatial perception, sustained attention, response speed); repeated or binge dosing was not tested (editors' count of tabulated studies: 16).
The reviewers' own comparisons of group means with norms are reported in a sentence each, without the norms, cut-offs or numbers; a group mean in the normal range does not show that individuals are.

hart_2012.locator: Main text, last paragraph before the metabolism studies
hart_2012.extracted: The term impairment is used both for a statistically significant group difference and for clinically meaningful loss of function; studies often report the first and discuss it as the second.

london_2015.extracted: Vervet monkeys given an escalating methamphetamine regimen had lower D2-type receptor and transporter availability (Groman et al., 2013, as summarized by the reviewers).

kish_2017.locator: Does Methamphetamine Cause Clinical Parkinsonism in the Human?, 2nd paragraph
kish_2017.extracted: Registry studies: California cohort HR 1.76 (95% CI 1.12–2.75) for Parkinson's disease versus an appendicitis group; Utah database HR 2.8 (1.6–4.8). The authors call these consistent with damage in a subgroup but not proof.

curtin_2015.extracted: Utah cohort: HR 2.8 (1.6–4.8) for a later Parkinson's disease code, 15 vs 27 events; see cl_meth_parkinson for the validity concerns.
4,935 people with a methamphetamine/amphetamine code vs 24,675 matched controls: 15 vs 27 Parkinson's disease events, HR 2.8 (95% CI 1.6–4.8); broader outcome 30 vs 49 events, HR 3.1.
Absolute risk of a Parkinson's code: 0.30% of the exposed cohort vs 0.11% of controls over a mean 6.8 years, about 2 extra cases per 1,000.

curtin_2015.locator: Table 1a, last two rows; Results §3.1, last paragraph
curtin_2015.extracted: For the broader movement-disorder outcome (30 exposed cases), median age at diagnosis 49 (range 25–69) vs 44 in controls, and a mean of 2.0 years (SD 1.8) from the first methamphetamine/amphetamine code; only 3 of 30 exposed cases had a carbidopa–levodopa order.

thompson_2004.locator: Results › Mapping cortical gray-matter deficits; Results › Hippocampal deficits
thompson_2004.extracted: 22 users vs 21 controls: grey-matter density 11.3% lower in the right cingulate (left 0.7%, not significant; medial frontal 3.6%, trend); hippocampal volume 7.8% smaller (p<0.01); total white matter 7.0% larger; total grey matter not different.

Users had 12.8 vs 15.2 years of education, 15 of 22 vs 2 of 21 smoked more than 5 cigarettes a day, and depression scores 9.77 vs 1.25 (editors' standardized differences about 1.1 for education and depression); none adjusted.

morales_2012.extracted: Control smokers had less grey matter than control non-smokers in the right orbitofrontal cortex; users (all smokers) had less grey matter than non-smoking controls in ten clusters, and than smoking controls in four (left superior temporal, right inferior temporal, right supramarginal, left precentral), only one of which has a same-named counterpart among the ten.

hart_2008.extracted: At 50 mg vs placebo: jittery 24.82 vs 7.36, sweating 25.09 vs 2.09, heart beating faster 43.18 vs 11.27, nose burning 28.00 vs 2.60 (all significant).

Dose effects are tested with denominator degrees of freedom of 330, 240 and 180, whereas 11 participants give 30 for a dose effect, so the printed p-values overstate precision; the differences in Table 1 are large enough that the direction of these effects is not in doubt.

glasner-edwards_2014.extracted: Little is known about antipsychotic safety and efficacy in children and adolescents with methamphetamine-induced psychosis.

The 16% and 17% figures come from two studies sharing their first five authors, and the remission-within-a-week statement in 5.1 carries no citation; the Thai figure is reported differently by two reviews (nearly 40% within 6 years; 38.8% at 5 years).

zorick_2010.extracted: The abstract says depressive and psychotic symptoms resolve within 1 week, which the Results do not support for depression; analyses use 25–32 of the 56 participants, and the numbers assessed at weeks 3–5 are not given.

cao_2026.locator: Abstract; Methods, Search Strategy; Results, Study Characteristics and Overall Cognitive Impairment
cao_2026.extracted: 68 studies published May 2017 to May 2025, 5244 users and 3801 controls: overall g −0.68 (95% CI −0.77 to −0.58), prediction interval −1.58 to 0.22.
The overall estimate pools 13 domains including self-reported impulsivity (g −0.86, 27 studies), a questionnaire rather than a performance test; GRADE certainty was very low for all 13 domains.

iudicello_2010.locator: Table 5; Results › Global Cognitive Functioning, 2nd–3rd paragraphs
iudicello_2010.extracted: Six abstainers impaired at baseline rose from 41.26 to 47.94 global T and six controls impaired at baseline from 43.70 to 47.01 (three-way interaction p=0.061); on processing speed (p=0.014) impaired abstainers rose 8.2 T while impaired controls fell 1.4 T, and on motor speed (p=0.051) 9.7 vs −0.1 T.

Abstinence was by self-report only and attrition from baseline is not reported; from Table 4 the follow-up abstainer–control difference gives p≈0.025 with the t-test the paper states it used, not the p>0.05 reported.
Over about a year, abstainers did not improve significantly more than retested controls (group × time p=0.126).

potvin_2018.extracted: Abstinence did not moderate global effect sizes (14 studies); weighted mean abstinence was 4.5 months.
Egger t=5.1, p=0.00003 for global cognition.

mcketin_2019.extracted: Any use vs no use: pooled unadjusted OR for psychosis 2.0 (95% CI 1.3–3.3), 7 studies, n=3436, I² 80%.
Average primary-study quality 68% of checklist items; the commonest shortfall was failure to identify and control confounders; publication bias was not assessed.

arunogiri_2018.locator: Results › Dose-amount and frequency of MA use; Table 2
arunogiri_2018.extracted: Frequency of use was associated with psychosis in 4 populations (odds 3–11 times higher in more frequent users) and not in 4; in the one prospective within-person cohort, months with 16 or more days of use had OR 11.2 (5.9–21.1) for psychotic symptoms, adjusted for other drug use.

arunogiri_2018.locator: Risk of bias within studies; Table 2
arunogiri_2018.extracted: In a systematic review of risk factors, this cohort was the only population rated in the top quality band; frequency of use was associated with psychosis in 4 of 8 populations.

bramness_2012.locator: Risk factors and acute vs. chronic psychosis, 5th paragraph
bramness_2012.extracted: Up to 25% of people first diagnosed with drug-induced psychosis develop a primary psychotic disorder, with higher figures for methamphetamine; a 2008 review found only 1 of 18 outcome papers with 1-year follow-up.

wearne_2018.locator: Positive symptoms › Acute meth psychosis vs. schizophrenia, 2nd paragraph
wearne_2018.extracted: Positive-symptom severity did not differ in most acute comparisons (PANSS: 9 vs 33 and 21 vs 14; BPRS among 198 people who use methamphetamine; PANSS at admission to 12 months in a prospective study).

wearne_2018.locator: Table 1 row 105; Positive symptoms › Chronic; Negative symptoms › Chronic
wearne_2018.extracted: Persistent psychosis beyond 1 month of abstinence (n=56) equalled schizophrenia (n=54) on BPRS total and positive scores, both above acute psychosis (n=50); negative symptoms schizophrenia > persistent > acute.

Acute and persistent cases are mixed, samples are small and medicated; Table 1 and the text disagree on group sizes and on whether visual and tactile hallucinations were more common in transient or persistent psychosis in one key study.

stockings_2019.extracted: Cause-of-death ascertainment was often unclear and polydrug use could not be examined; older cohorts probably involved amphetamine rather than crystalline methamphetamine; the headline ratio appears as 6.83, 6.3, 6.2 and 6.08 in different places.

trivedi_2021.extracted: Complete-case analysis: 28.8% vs 5.1% and 16.2% vs 1.3%; only 47.7% of the stage 1 active group provided all four samples, so missing samples, counted as non-response, were common.

trivedi_2021.locator: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03078075 › Primary Outcome Measures; Study Record Dates
trivedi_2021.extracted: Registered before enrolment; the registry lists the two stage-specific responses, while the article's primary outcome is their weighted combination, prespecified in the protocol's analysis plan.

basterfield_2019.extracted: The authors conclude that strong statements about impaired cognition in abstinent users are premature because cross-sectional designs cannot separate pre-existing differences from drug effects.

simon_2010.extracted: The composite difference at baseline (−0.31 vs 0.01) became non-significant when years of education was entered as a covariate.
